newsitem.title: BRAZIL: FOCUS - Brazil forges ahead with telecoms overhaul.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Brazil forges ahead with telecoms overhaul.

text.p: While expected by the market, lower house approval of a new telecommunications law Wednesday showed Brazil was forging ahead with the transformation of its massive telecoms sector, analysts said.
"The process is unfolding. That's the good news," said Rodrigo Fiaes of local bank Banco Icatu.
The legislation, which faces Senate approval, regulates and creates a watchdog for the sector and authorizes the privatization of the federal Telebras system.
Local stock markets were not surprised by the Chamber of Deputies' passage of the General Telecommunications Law and at least four government-backed amendments to the bill.
"This was already mostly factored into prices. It's positive but it won't affect the markets," said Jacopo Valentino of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Still, its passage comes amid the privatization of B Band cellular concessions, lending momentum to the change overtaking the mostly state-owned sector, analysts said.
The chamber also rejected a fifth amendment floated by the opposition to keep rates under state control.
The bill aims to create regulations and a watchdog agency modeled after U.S. and British systems. It would allow companies to set their own rates after a three-year transition period.
Analysts said the proposed law should result in more competitive, efficient telecoms service and lower rates to replace the existing and costly state-run system.
Currently, it can take months to get a telephone line installed by Telebras' state-level operating subsidiaries.

Deputies are expected to continue voting over the next few days on further amendments, including a proposal to limit foreign capital stakes in new private telecoms. But the amendments are not expected to seriously affect future foreign telecoms investment in Brazil.

"Investors are going to jump on any telecoms privatizations in Brazil," Icatu's Fiaes said. "Things are happening here. They're not happening in China or India. So this is the place to be in telecoms in emerging markets."

Events are likely to move quickly after Wednesday's vote, with the creation of a watchdog agency likely to come shortly after President Fernando Henrique Cardoso signs the bill into law. Analysts said that could happen as early as next month.

"I expect the law to be on the books in late July," Fiaes said. "The fine details of the watchdog are well under way so the government is likely to announce the regulator's creation before the end of the year or early in 1998."
